results.summary: This design implements a motocross racing game for up to four players, each controlling a bike with a single button. It outputs a VGA signal to display the game track and uses bidirectional pins to select among four tracks and set game speed. The design is notable for supporting four simultaneous players with minimal controls and is based on an open-source project.

This analog design implements a voltage-controlled ring oscillator with an 8-bit DAC for frequency tuning. It uses input pins to select the image and control color, and outputs standard VGA signals. The design is notable for its trimming capability and analog implementation.

This design implements a robust finite state machine that handles a custom UART protocol for real-time configuration and data reporting. It uses a UART interface for communication and includes a protocol FSM for handling data. The design is notable for its robust protocol handling and real-time capabilities.

This design implements a multiplier and CORDIC algorithm using SPI interface. It uses approximate computing techniques for area and power savings. The design is notable for its use of approximate computing and SPI interface.

This design implements a finite state machine with SPI interface and ADC for radio applications. It includes memory and sensor interface for data acquisition. The design is notable for its integration of multiple functions in a single design.

This design receives serial data via UART, stores it in an 8-bit register, and compares it with a pseudo-random pattern generated by an LFSR. It uses an LFSR for pattern generation and a comparator for detection. The design is notable for its use of LFSR and UART interface.

This design implements a traffic light controller as a finite state machine, using an instantiated clock frequency divider for timing. It uses a clock divider to generate timing signals for the traffic light sequence. The design is notable for its use of a clock divider and FSM.

This design implements a bandgap voltage reference with analog output. It uses transistor-level implementation for precision. The design is notable for its trimming capability and analog implementation.

This design implements a voltage-controlled ring oscillator with an 8-bit DAC for frequency tuning. It uses analog input for frequency control. The design is notable for its analog implementation and DAC.

This design implements a counter that generates clock signals with divided frequencies. It uses a counter to divide the input clock frequency. The design is notable for its frequency division capability.
